prompt: A SCIENCE-FAIR physics demonstration on a lab table: a straight rigid plank balancing on a single central triangular pivot (fulcrum), shown straight on from the side, set up to teach the lever rule. The plank has evenly spaced distance marks numbered 1 to 6 outward from the pivot on BOTH sides (mark 1 is one step out, mark 2 two steps, and so on). Every cube weight block is IDENTICAL in weight. On the LEFT of the pivot, stack 5 RED cube blocks centred exactly on distance mark 2. On the RIGHT of the pivot you must place 2 BLUE cube blocks -- and you must choose WHICH distance mark to put them on so the plank BALANCES perfectly level. Use the lever rule: (number of blocks on a side) x (their distance mark) must be EQUAL on the two sides. Work out the correct right-hand mark for the 2 blue blocks, place all 2 of them centred on that mark, and draw the plank exactly LEVEL (horizontal) because it is balanced. Clean demo-table setting, the numbered marks clearly visible, no extra objects or text.
